title: 2003 AMC 8 Problem 4
statement: A group of children riding on bicycles and tricycles rode past Billy Bob’s house. Billy Bob counted \(7\) children and \(19\) wheels. How many tricycles were there?

solutions.text:
Let \(b\) be the number of bicycles and \(t\) be the number of tricycles. Then we can set up the following system of equations: \[ \begin{gather*} b + t = 7, \\ 2b + 3t = 19. \end{gather*} \] Multiplying the first equation by \(2\) and subtracting from the second equation, we get \(t = 5.\)

Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: If all \(7\) children had bicycles, count the wheels.
Each tricycle adds one wheel compared with a bicycle.
